claims.claim: Finite-sequence survival with unrotatable dominoes is in NP.
claims.evidence: For each explicitly listed piece, a certificate gives its locking position. From the reconstructed board, reachability is decidable by graph search over O(WH) fixed-orientation positions; locking, loss, placement, and simultaneous row deletion are directly checkable. Repeating this for all pieces is polynomial in the explicit board and sequence sizes.
claims.witness: A certificate consisting of one locking coordinate per piece, verified by per-piece reachability searches.
claims.search_method: Direct complexity analysis of the source movement and clearing rules.

claims.claim: For row-parallel unrotatable dominoes on an odd-width board, there is a computable linear-size upper bound on the number of pieces that can ever survive.
claims.evidence: A row token retains its initial occupied barriers until it clears, so it accepts at most c_i=sum floor(ell/2) horizontal pieces and can clear only when all its initial empty intervals have even length. Only the q such initial tokens can clear. Each resulting fresh odd-width empty token never clears and accepts at most m=floor(W/2) pieces. Hence every play has length at most U=C+qm<=H(W-1), computable in O(WH).
claims.witness: The row-token invariant and explicit bound U=C+q floor(W/2).
claims.search_method: First-principles invariant proof, supplemented by exhaustive bounded state-space enumeration.

claims.claim: On an odd-width board with arbitrary mixed fixed orientations, every survivable prefix obeys a computable horizontal-versus-vertical obstruction h <= C + m b(v) <= U + (W-1)v.
claims.evidence: Every odd initial empty interval in a cleared initial token needs a distinct vertical endpoint, as does every cleared fresh odd-width token. Thus sum_{R in S} d(R)+z<=2v. This gives at most q+2v clears when q>0, and at most 2v-delta+1 after the delta-endpoint startup cost when q=0. Initial tokens accept at most C horizontal pieces and each of the resulting fresh tokens at most m, proving both displayed inequalities.
claims.witness: An injective charge from every required odd-interval correction to one of the 2v vertical-domino cells.
claims.search_method: Symbolic endpoint-charge audit plus exhaustive exploration of 35,529 bounded reachable mixed states.

claims.claim: The coefficient W-1 in the mixed odd-width obstruction is asymptotically sharp: on every initially empty odd W by H board with W>=3 and H>=3, the block consisting of one vertical domino followed by W-1 horizontal dominoes can be repeated indefinitely.
claims.evidence: Put the vertical domino in an outer column of the bottom two rows. The first m horizontals tile the other W-1 bottom cells and clear that row; the surviving upper vertical cell then occupies the bottom outer cell. Another m horizontals clear that row and restore the empty board. The top corridor remains available because H>=3, so the cycle repeats and has h/v=W-1.
claims.witness: The exact cycle V H^(W-1), returning to the empty board after every block.
claims.search_method: Constructive proof and exact checks for W=3,5,7 across all 68 tested horizontal-edge and vertical-column spawn choices.

claims.claim: On an even-width board, two initially empty top rows suffice for survival of arbitrarily many row-parallel unrotatable dominoes.
claims.evidence: Partition the columns into adjacent pairs. Capping each pair equalizes its two column tops without occupying the top row. Raise all lower pair tops to the maximum pair top; either a row clears earlier or the maximum row becomes full. In either case, the previously empty top row shifts below a newly inserted empty row, restoring two empty top rows and permitting another phase.
claims.search_method: Constructive invariant audit plus reachable-cycle checks on 243 bounded even-width boards.

claims.claim: On any height-at-least-three board with no complete row and two empty top rows, every finite all-vertical unrotatable-domino sequence is survivable.
claims.evidence: Let T be the greatest column height and raise each column by vertical dominoes to T or T+1 according to its height parity. Unless a row clears earlier, every column then occupies row T-1, forcing a clear. High final lifts are reachable by placing corridor-blocking columns farthest-to-nearest from the spawn column and the spawn column last. The top row remains empty, so every clear restores two empty top rows; the no-complete-row premise ensures each phase is nonempty.
claims.witness: The column-parity leveling phase, with an empty-board phase that raises every column to height two.
claims.search_method: Constructive reachability audit plus exact reachable-cycle checks on 75 bounded boards.

claims.claim: Two empty top rows do not suffice for arbitrary mixed orientations: on the empty 4×3 board with centered horizontal spawn, the fixed sequence VHHHH is not survivable, irrespective of the vertical spawn column.
claims.evidence: After V falls, each of the bottom two rows has one occupied cell. Each can accept at most one horizontal domino and cannot become full, so the third H must lock in the top row. Every horizontal edge of a width-four top row intersects the centered spawn pair in columns 2-3; that nonfull top lock blocks the fourth H. The argument is independent of V's final column.
claims.witness: The empty 4x3 board with sequence VHHHH and centered horizontal spawn.
claims.search_method: Complete parity-and-spawn case analysis, confirmed by exact search for all four vertical spawn columns.

claims.claim: The maximum survival length on an initially empty odd-width W×H board with row-parallel unrotatable dominoes is exactly H floor(W/2).
claims.evidence: Horizontal placements preserve even occupancy in each initially empty row, so no odd-width row can clear and each row contains at most floor(W/2) dominoes. Every edge of an odd path belongs to a maximum matching. Choosing a maximum matching containing the spawn edge and repeating it bottom-to-top attains the bound; on the top row, placing the other matching edges outward-to-inward and the spawn edge last preserves access.
claims.witness: A maximum matching of each row containing the fixed spawn edge, repeated through all H levels.
claims.search_method: Parity upper bound, explicit matching construction, and exact maximum-length checks on eight bounded dimensions.

claims.claim: The row-capacity bound is not sufficient, and clearing one row does not guarantee indefinite unrotatable-domino survival.
claims.evidence: On the 3x3 board .../.#./..., U=2 but either first horizontal domino locks in the top row and intersects every possible width-three spawn edge, so only one piece survives. On the 3x2 board .../..#, the first domino clears the bottom row, leaving an empty odd-width board whose exact remaining capacity is two; therefore three pieces survive but four do not.
claims.witness: The boards .../.#./... and .../..# with exact maximum lengths one and three respectively.
claims.search_method: Direct geometric analysis and exact state-space computation of both witnesses.

claims.claim: Two initially empty top rows cannot in general be weakened to one on even-width row-parallel boards.
claims.evidence: On the 4x2 board ..../#... with centered spawn, the first domino either blocks the next spawn from the top or leaves a bottom row with no adjacent empty pair. In the latter cases, the second domino must lock in the top row. Every top-row horizontal edge intersects the centered spawn pair, so a third piece cannot spawn. Thus one empty top row does not guarantee indefinite survival.
claims.witness: The 4x2 board top/bottom=..../#..., which has maximum survival length two.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive first- and second-placement case analysis, confirmed by exact state search.

claims.claim: For odd-width row-parallel instances whose completely empty initial rows form a top prefix, finite clearing polynomial-time many-one reduces to finite survival.
claims.evidence: A clearing play must use exactly K0 pieces in nonempty initial tokens and requires all their empty intervals to be even; otherwise the instance is immediately NO. In the remaining case, map to survival for L=K0+Hm pieces. Clearing implies survival by appending the empty-board construction. Conversely, L saturates the token bound, forcing every nonempty initial token to clear. Empty-origin tokens always remain above those tokens, so deleting their placements removes no support and only removes obstacles, yielding a valid K0-piece clearing play. The output length is O(WH).
claims.witness: The map (B,K0) -> (B,L=K0+H floor(W/2)), with fixed NO output for preprocessing failures.
claims.search_method: Reduction soundness/completeness audit plus exhaustive equivalence checks on 1,271 bounded promised boards.
